correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, endpoint differences give the two k^-2 tails, and folding and reflection prove exact vanishing in each inactive nonconstant parity. The uniform interior alias remainder is O(N^-2) after scaling. The fixed positive-frequency terms needed to exclude active edge indices are strictly positive by Abel summation (first positive partial sum) and the strictly decreasing sine-integral weight; a positive even mass supplies a positive mean. At an inactive odd-grid edge all nonconstant active aliases have |k| at least N-j after reflection, so the uniform tail bound extends to the edge and gives nD/2. The constant case gives zero, and minimization of the interior profiles gives both stated constants. The supplied finite checks were inspected, not executed, and are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The frozen attribution of global strictness and exact cyclic ranks as contributions does not pass: an earlier arbitrary-node nullity theorem covers both, and also gives the endpoint tail. The corrected files limit the new claim to the sharp even/odd least-eigenvalue limits. Neither the verified nullity theorem, which identifies kernels, nor the preservation theorem quantifies these limits; alias splitting and edge control are needed. The fixed-degree all-frequency sign refinement is used in the proof, not promoted as the main novelty.
residual_risks: A bounded search cannot exclude an older equivalent covariance-sampling or periodic-spline formula. No claim of novelty for the tail or rank classification remains.

value.rationale: The repaired quantitative bounds determine the conditioning scale that nullity alone cannot predict. In particular the same single-parity kernel has an exactly singular large even grid yet a positive odd-grid inverse-size constant, and with both masses active the explicit gap can be significant. The result is motivated by stable covariance sampling and captures all fixed Bernstein inputs, not a choice of isolated parameters.
